text.p: Food distributor Krantor Corp said Tuesday it foresaw a profit of $100,000 or $.004 a share for the first quarter of 1997, ending March 31, 1997.
The company said it also saw a profit of $550,000 or $.022 a share for fiscal 1997. Discontinued operations would not have a "negative impact" on the results, it added.
For the 1996 first quarter, the company reported a net loss of $265,100, or $0.05 a share.
The company said that for the 1996 fourth quarter, it would likely report a profit from continuing operations in excess of $100,000 on revenues of $323,928.
"This marks the first time since the third quarter of 1995 in which the company has achieved a profit from continuing operations," it said.
Krantor said revenues from continuing operations for 1996 totalled $7.4 million, with a loss of less than $300,000.
Krantor expects to release its 1996 results by April 15.

"The company expects to enhance its revenue base by representing manufacturers and service providers to its retail customer base," it said. "The company believes that its contacts and relationships with major retail food customers in the Northeast should produce revenue growth in the near future.
"The company may still need to resolve some on-going litigation matters related to the closure of its Kosher business," it added.
Krantor is an agent for a China-based trading company distributing frozen seafood and brand name grocery products to major retailers and wholesalers in the eastern United States.
